name: intlMsg / intlNumber / intlDateTime and formatters
summary: Format locale-aware values without coupling output to custom elements.

npm.import: import { intlMsg, intlNumber, intlDateTime, intlDuration, intlRelTime, intlList, intlName, intlPlural } from '@beforesemicolon/intl/formatters'
npm.registration: No custom elements register when importing this subpath.

classic.registration: The script registers its custom elements automatically.

signatures.intlMsg: (key: string, values?: MessageValues, options?: MessageFormatOptions) => string
signatures.intlDateTime: (value: string | number | Date, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions & FormatterOptions) => string
signatures.intlList: (value: string[] | string, options?: ListFormatOptions & FormatterOptions) => string

example.npm:
import { intlNumber } from '@beforesemicolon/intl/formatters'
console.log(intlNumber(1200, { locale: 'en-US', style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }))

guidance: Use the formatter subpath when you do not need custom elements. In classic mode use BFS.INTL.
Pass an explicit scope when formatting outside the top-level application. Native Intl options are used where applicable.
Format functions take the value as the first argument. Do not pass an object with a value field as shown in older examples.
